we identified the coding region for MCP in the HindIII U fragment of HCMV and that we expressed the MCP in Escherichian coli and used it to generate polyclonl antibodies.
the major capsid proteins of HCMV and simian cytomega- lovirus are related and that the gene for this protein is located in the HindIII U fragment.
the coding region for MCP of human cytomeglavirus was identified and the corresponding gene product was detected by using monoclonal antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the major capsids of HCMV and simian cytomegalo virus.
the identification and characterization of the HCM V MCP.
a new method of identifying genes by comparison of protein sequences of different viruses and by the application of monoclonal antibodies and antisera against the respective proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HCMV gene encoding the major capsid polypeptide was identified.
the HCMV gene for the major capsids is the HindIII fragment U.
the HCMV major capsid protein is encoded by the HindIII U fragment and that the coding sequence is located in the HindIII B fragment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HCMV major capsid protein is a protein of 1,370 to 1,390 amino acid residues and that the HCMVP5 gene is located on HindIII fragment U of HCMV.
the HCMV major capsid protein has a length of 1,370 residues, a molecular weight of about 155 kilodaltons, and a calculated isoelectric point of 4.7.
the HCMV major capsid protein is a 1,370-amino-acid polypeptide and is encoded by a 8-kilobase transcript.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HCMV capsid protein gene has been cloned and characterized.
we have identified the coding region for a protein of 1,370 residues, which we have designated the HCMV major capsid protein.
the MCP of HCMV can be used as a target antigen in serologic tests.
